key_insight: A transferred monolayer graphene contact improved AlInN/Si solar cell performance by increasing current collection and fill factor without materially changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature transparent conductive contact to boost nitride-based solar cells while preserving compatibility with Si-based device integration.
method: Built AlxIn1−xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with an a-Si buffer layer to improve the heterointerface.
Tested three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact and compared devices with/without graphene under dark and illuminated conditions.
evidence_signal: Across all three compositions, the abstract reports higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency after graphene integration, with open-circuit voltage largely unchanged.
watch_item: The benefit depends on a successful graphene transfer and contact uniformity, so scalability, interface quality, and process repeatability need verification.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
